manuscript_sha256.description: sha256 of the audited manuscript's bytes — the case folder's content identity. Absent on manifests written before content hashing, which fall back to comparing the file name.

boundary_ambiguous.description: True when the reference label occurred more than once before the next reference, so the entry's start is a guess. Such an entry is never resolved: nothing derived from its text may be trusted to name a paper.

title_check.description: Whether anyone established that the retrieved or provided file is the paper the reference names. 'unverifiable' (e.g. a scanned first page) is not 'verified' and must never be reported as a match.

references_resumed.description: True when the reference list was picked up again after an intervening section, so the entry numbering spans a boundary the parser chose to cross. Gated on block type and run length, but still a judgement — the reader should be able to check it.

reference_source.description: Which reading of the reference list these entries came from: the publisher's list deposited with Crossref, or the tool's own parse of the PDF text. Absent on manifests written before reconciliation, which are all parses.

numbering_verified.description: True when the chosen list accounts for exactly the labels the manuscript's body cites. The label is the join key between a claim and its source, so an unverified numbering means a verdict may be about a different paper than the label names. Absent on older manifests, which never checked.

numbering_note.description: Why the numbering was or was not confirmed, in the reader's terms — the counts each reading produced and what the body cites.

unverified_from.description: The first citation label from which the numbering is in doubt, or null when it is not in doubt. 1 means 'from the very start', which is what a single unchecked reading warrants: one candidate gives no evidence about where it went wrong.
